ei.title: Theories and Practices of Sports Fandom
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective. From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team. There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory. Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique. These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership. Sports team supporters are one such group. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members. This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams. This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs. Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way. This phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for their sports teams. People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well. Even though a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits, the mere act of watching the game brings them satisfaction. This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams. Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases. However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions. Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges. It can also have positive effects on our brains. For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal. If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater. So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses. While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people. Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams. When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game. Typically, the cheers from the home team’s fans are louder than those from the visiting team’s supporters. This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021. The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches. It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums. It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor. Sports fandom can be analyzed using both evolutionary and social psychological approaches. Through these perspectives, we can understand why people have loyalty and support for their teams. Given that sports fandom has become more and more common in modern times, we should think about our role as fans. We should establish a healthy culture of fandom and seek ways to practice fandom that can have a positive influence on society.

questions.passage: If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy.  In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, ①<u>which</u> overly aggressive support of their team sometimes ②<u>leads</u> to confrontations with fans from opposition teams.  If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger ③<u>emerge</u> from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal?  What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan?  And would their passion and cheering actually ④<u>influence</u> the performance of their team?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① which → whose: 뒤의 명사 support가 fans의 소유임을 나타내므로 소유격 관계대명사 whose
det.analysis:
❌ ① which → whose: 'extreme fans, ___ overly aggressive support of their team'에서 뒤의 명사 support가 앞의 fans에게 '속한' 것이다. 이렇게 '~의'라는 소유 관계를 나타내며 명사 앞에 오는 관계대명사는 whose다. which는 뒤에 바로 명사를 이끌 수 없어 틀리다 ← 정답

✅ ② leads: 주어가 'whose overly aggressive support(단수)'이므로 단수 동사 leads로 적절

✅ ③ emerge: 주어가 'joy, sadness, and even anger(복수)'이므로 복수 동사 emerge로 적절

✅ ④ influence: 조동사 would 뒤에 오는 동사원형 influence로 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 명사가 바로 오며 소유(~의)를 나타내면 whose: fans whose support(팬들의 응원)

questions.passage: There are also two social psychological theories that might ①<u>explain</u> why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory.  Though it may be human nature ②<u>to form</u> a group and ③<u>feeling a sense of belonging</u> to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends.  Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation.  That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique.  These two basic but competing needs can be ④<u>satisfied</u> through group membership.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ feeling → feel: 앞의 to form과 and로 대등하게 연결되는 병렬 구조이므로 (to) feel
det.analysis:
✅ ① explain: 조동사 might 뒤에 오는 동사원형 explain으로 적절

✅ ② to form: 'human nature to form a group(집단을 이루는 인간 본성)'에서 명사를 꾸미는 to부정사로 적절

❌ ③ feeling → feel: 'human nature to form a group and ___ a sense of belonging'에서 and는 앞의 to form과 대등한 것을 연결한다. 따라서 to form과 짝을 이루는 (to) feel이 와야 한다. feeling은 병렬이 깨져 틀리다 ← 정답

✅ ④ satisfied: 'These two ~ needs can be satisfied'에서 욕구가 '충족되는' 대상이므로 수동태의 과거분사로 적절
det.tip: A and B 병렬: to form a group and (to) feel a sense of belonging

questions.passage: For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may ①<u>release</u> dopamine.  Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” ②<u>make you feel</u> pleasure when you reach a goal.  If you have ③<u>pursued</u> the goal for a long time, the effect is greater.  So it is a particular thrill when a team ④<u>achieves</u> victory following a series of back-to-back losses.  While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② make → makes: 주어가 Dopamine(단수)이므로 단수 동사 makes
det.analysis:
✅ ① release: 조동사 may 뒤에 오는 동사원형 release로 적절

❌ ② make → makes: 'Dopamine, a chemical known as the "happy hormone," ___ you feel pleasure'에서 진짜 주어는 Dopamine(단수)이다. 사이에 낀 'a chemical known as ~'는 삽입된 설명일 뿐이다. 단수 주어에는 makes를 써야 하므로 make는 틀리다 ← 정답

✅ ③ pursued: 'If you have pursued the goal'에서 현재완료(have p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사로 적절

✅ ④ achieves: 'when a team achieves victory'에서 주어 a team(단수)에 맞는 단수 동사로 적절
det.tip: 삽입어구(a chemical ~)에 속지 말고 진짜 주어(Dopamine, 단수)에 동사를 맞추기: makes

questions.passage: Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation.  That is, individuals want to be ①<u>included</u> somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique.  These two basic but ②<u>competing</u> needs can be satisfied through group membership. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ similar to → different from: 우리 팀 팬은 다른 팀 팬과 '다르기에' 특별함을 느낌
det.analysis:
✅ ① included: '어딘가에 속하고(included) 싶어 한다'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② competing: 소속과 차별화라는 '서로 경쟁하는(competing)' 두 욕구라는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ satisfy: '소속 욕구를 충족할(satisfy) 수 있다'는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ similar to(비슷한) → different from(다른): 원문은 'your team's fans are different from the fans of other teams'로, 우리 팀 팬이 다른 팀 팬과 '다르기' 때문에 특별함을 느낀다는 뜻이다. similar(비슷한)은 정반대라 특별함(uniqueness)이라는 흐름과 맞지 않는다 ← 정답
det.tip: 특별함(unique)을 느끼는 이유는 다른 팀 팬과 different(다르기) 때문

questions.passage: Supporting a team ①<u>passionately</u> can help people ②<u>remember</u> about their daily life challenges.  It can also have positive effects on our brains.  For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② remember → forget: 열정적 응원은 일상의 어려움을 '잊게' 도와줌
det.analysis:
✅ ① passionately: '팀을 열정적으로(passionately) 응원하는 것'이라는 문맥에 적절

❌ ② remember(기억하다) → forget(잊다): 원문은 'help people forget about their daily life challenges'로, 응원이 일상의 어려움을 '잊도록' 돕는다는 뜻이다. remember(기억하다)는 정반대라 스트레스 해소라는 긍정적 효과와 맞지 않는다 ← 정답

✅ ③ greater: '오래 추구한 목표일수록 효과가 더 크다(greater)'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ thrill: '연속 패배 뒤 승리는 특별한 짜릿함(thrill)'이라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 응원은 일상의 어려움을 forget(잊게) 도와줌 — remember(기억)가 아님

questions.passage: For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine.  Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal.  If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater.  So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of __________.  While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에는 '연속된 패배(back-to-back losses)'가 적절
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of ___.'(그래서 팀이 일련의 ___ 뒤에 승리를 거둘 때 특별히 짜릿하다). 앞에서 '오래 추구한 목표일수록 효과가 크다'고 했고, 승리가 더 짜릿하려면 그 앞이 힘든 상황이어야 한다.

❌ ① last-minute goals(막판 골): 패배의 연속이라는 대비가 없어 짜릿함의 이유가 약하다.

❌ ② home-field advantages(홈 이점): 뒤의 victory와 대비되는 고난이 아니다.

✅ ③ back-to-back losses(연속된 패배): 연속 패배 뒤의 승리라 더욱 짜릿하다는 흐름과 딱 맞는다 ← 정답

❌ ④ long practice sessions(긴 연습): 패배와 대비되는 고난의 의미가 아니다.
det.tip: victory following a series of ___ : 승리와 대비되는 back-to-back losses(연속 패배)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에는 '상호 협력(mutual cooperation)'이 적절
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'People could help each other in groups ~. This ___ built trust and fostered relationships among group members.'(사람들은 집단 안에서 서로 도울 수 있었다. 이 ___이 신뢰를 쌓고 관계를 길렀다). 앞에서 '서로 도왔다(help each other)'고 했으므로 빈칸은 그것을 가리켜야 한다.

✅ ① mutual cooperation(상호 협력): 서로 돕는 것을 그대로 받아 신뢰를 쌓았다는 흐름과 딱 맞는다 ← 정답

❌ ② fierce competition(치열한 경쟁): 신뢰를 쌓는 흐름과 반대다.

❌ ③ personal ambition(개인적 야망): 집단 내 협력이라는 문맥과 어긋난다.

❌ ④ sheer luck(순전한 운): 서로 도운 행동의 결과가 아니다.
det.tip: help each other(서로 돕다)를 받는 말 → mutual cooperation(상호 협력)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 진화적 관점에서의 집단과 생존.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago'에서 수만 년 전 조상에게서 비롯되었으므로 '몇백 년 전 도시화'는 불일치

❌ ② 본문 'far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual'에서 집단의 일원이 더 유리했으므로 반대

❌ ③ 본문 'tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat ~'에서 강한 공동체가 이겼으므로 '불리했다'는 불일치

✅ ④ 본문 'the instinct to find one's own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people'와 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: 본능은 현대인에게 passed down(전해졌다). 나머지는 방향이 뒤집혀 있습니다.

ch: 스포츠 팬덤은 겨우 몇백 년 전 도시화와 함께 처음 생겨났다.

자기 집단을 찾으려는 본능은 조상에게서 현대인에게로 전해졌다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 소속·차별화 욕구와 반사된 영광.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team'과 일치

✅ ② 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 본문 'This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams' deliberate use of their team colors and songs.'에서 팀 색과 응원가는 특별함(소속감의 독특성)을 '강화한다(reinforced)'고 했다. '약화시킨다'는 정반대다 ← 정답

❌ ④ 본문 'People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well'과 일치
det.tip: 팀 색·응원가는 특별함을 reinforced(강화)합니다. 약화가 아닙니다.

ch: 자신의 도시를 연고로 하는 팀을 응원하면 소속 욕구를 채울 수 있다.
팀 색과 응원가는 팬들의 소속감을 약화시키는 역할을 한다.
반사된 영광 누리기는 타인의 성공과 자신을 연결해 성공감을 느끼는 것이다.
팬들은 자기 팀이 이기거나 좋은 경기를 하면 자부심을 느낀다.

det.korean: 2021년 연구의 내용.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'it may not be the determining factor'에서 응원이 '결정적 요인은 아닐 수 있다'고 했으므로 '유일한 요인'은 불일치

❌ ② 본문 'home matches in an Italian football league'에서 이탈리아 리그이므로 '스페인 리그'는 불일치

✅ ③ 본문 'The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches'와 일치 ← 정답

❌ ④ 본문 'during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums'에서 팬데믹 때 관중이 입장 '금지'되었으므로 '자유롭게 입장'은 불일치
det.tip: 연구는 cheering과 goals의 관계를 살폈습니다. 리그(이탈리아)·입장 금지를 대조하세요.

ch: 응원은 팀의 성과를 결정짓는 유일한 요인으로 확인되었다.
2021년 연구는 스페인 리그의 경기를 분석 대상으로 삼았다.
그 연구는 응원과 경기에서 득점된 골 사이의 관계를 살펴보았다.
팬데믹 기간에도 관중은 자유롭게 경기장에 입장할 수 있었다.

If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal?  What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan?  And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team?  These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.  From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago.
